question.problem: At which points on the curve $2xy+3{y}^{2}={x}^{2}+4$ is the tangent vector to the curve perpendicular to the vector $j?$
question.worked_solution:
First, we bring all variables to one side:

$$
\begin{aligned}2xy+3{y}^{2} & ={x}^{2}+4 \\ 2xy+3{y}^{2}-{x}^{2} & =4\end{aligned}
$$

If we set $f(x,y)=2xy+3{y}^{2}-{x}^{2}$, our curve can be viewed as the level curve $f(x,y)=4.$ 

A tangent vector to the level curve can be computed as follows:

$$
t(x,y)={f}_{y}(x,y)\,i-{f}_{x}(x,y)\,j
$$

So, we calculate $t(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}t(x,y) & ={f}_{y}(x,y)\,i-{f}_{x}(x,y)\,j \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2xy+3{y}^{2}-{x}^{2})\,i-\frac{∂}{∂x}(2xy+3{y}^{2}-{x}^{2})\,j \\  & =(2x+6y)\,i-(2y-2x)\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Since our tangent vector needs to be perpendicular to $j$, we must have $t\cdot j=0.$

$$
\begin{aligned}t(x,y)\cdot j & =0 \\ ((2x+6y)\,i-(2y-2x)\,j)\cdot j & =0 \\ 2y-2x & =0 \\ y & =x\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $y=x$ into the equation of our curve gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}2xy+3{y}^{2} & ={x}^{2}+4 \\ 2x(x)+3(x)^{2} & ={x}^{2}+4 \\ 2{x}^{2}+3{x}^{2} & ={x}^{2}+4 \\ 4{x}^{2} & =4 \\ {x}^{2} & =1 \\ x & =\pm 1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally:

- If $x=1$, we get $y=1$ and the corresponding point is $(1,1).$

- If $x=-1$, we get $y=-1$ and the corresponding point is $(-1,-1).$
